Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

## Fault Localization

1. The test `MetaphoneTest.testLocaleIndependence()` in the class `MetaphoneTest` is failing.
2. The test method tests the locale independence of a `StringEncoder` by encoding some data with different locales and comparing the results.
3. The test sets different locales (`Locale.ENGLISH`, `new Locale("tr") and the default locale) and encodes the data with the `StringEncoder`.
4. There is a comparison between the encoded strings with different locales. The encoded string is stored in `ref` when `j <= 0` and compared with the encoded string in `cur` when `j > 0`.

## Hypothesis

Based on the current bug report mentioning "Fix case-insensitive string handling" and the test method's comparison of encoded strings with different locales, I suspect that the issue might be related to case sensitivity in string encoding or comparison in different locales.

I will now inspect the relevant method `StringEncoder.encode(String)` to understand how the encoding is performed and how the comparison of encoded strings is done.

The `StringEncoder.encode(String)` method signature is `String encode(String pString) throws EncoderException`. This method takes a `String` as input and returns an encoded `String`.

Next, I will examine the implementation of the `StringEncoder.encode(String)` method to identify any issues related to case sensitivity in string handling.
